$comment: Extra glossary terms for the building-agents concept briefs (part file `build`). Each definition follows Microsoft Learn. Ids here are not defined in terms.json or any other part file.

hook.plain: a rule that runs a workflow every time a set moment happens in an agent's work, such as before a tool runs

primary-agent.plain: the main agent that talks with the person and hands focused work to other agents

agents-sdk.plain: a developer toolkit for building agents in code that can work in Teams, on websites, and in other places

a2a.plain: an open standard that lets agents from different makers send tasks to each other

sandbox.plain: a protected area where code runs, kept apart from the rest of the system

code-interpreter.plain: a tool that lets an AI write and run Python code to analyze data and make files

markdown.plain: a simple way to format text, such as headings and lists, by using plain characters

custom-connector.plain: a connector you define for your own service when no ready-made connector exists

data-gateway.plain: a program on your own network that lets cloud services reach local data without opening inbound ports

virtual-network.plain: a private network in Azure; with it, Power Platform can reach private resources without the public internet

work-iq.plain: a Microsoft 365 layer that gives agents real-time work context, such as mail, calendar, and files, within your permissions

activity-map.plain: a view in the test chat that shows which topics, tools, or sources the agent picked for a reply

context-window.plain: the amount of information an agent can use at one time

autonomous-agent.plain: an agent that runs when an event happens in a connected service, not only when a person chats

escalation.plain: handing a conversation to a human representative when the agent cannot resolve it

contact-center.plain: the team and systems that handle customer calls and chats

vector-store.plain: a search store that holds your files so an agent can search them by keywords and by meaning

toolbox.plain: a managed set of tools in Foundry that many agents share through one endpoint

typespec.plain: a text language for describing an agent and its actions, which the toolkit turns into the agent's manifest

manifest.plain: a file that describes an agent, such as its name, instructions, knowledge, and actions

api-plugin.plain: an action that lets a declarative agent call a web service described by an OpenAPI file

oauth.plain: a standard sign-in method that lets an app act for a person without handling their password

starter-prompt.plain: a suggested question on an agent that shows people what it can do

azure-ai-search.plain: a search service that indexes your content so apps and agents can find it

managed-identity.plain: an identity Azure gives a service so it can sign in to other services without a stored password

temperature.plain: a setting from 0 to 1 that makes a model's answers more predictable or more varied

copilot-connector.plain: a connector that brings content from another system into Microsoft 365 so Copilot and its agents can use it

embedded-file.plain: a file you upload from your device so it becomes part of an agent's knowledge

activity-protocol.plain: the messaging standard Copilot Studio uses to talk to a connected Foundry agent
